thread:
Indra: Quick sync on model header v2 — need a compact contract that supports: cheap existence checks, range/index pointers for gzipped bundles, per-shard digests, and a reader-lease token so evictions don't race active readers. Thinking: keep header <= 4KB for fast probe.
Sam: Curious about gzipped bundles: we still need a separate range index to serve byte ranges from compressed files, right? If so the header should point to a small "range_index_digest" rather than embed offsets.
Jia: Yep. My idea: header fields = version, format, total_shards, shard_id (optional), manifest_digest, range_index_digest (opt), flags, min_loader_version, capset (bitlist), signed_lease_pubkey. Keep it tiny.
Clare: How do leases work in practice? We want cheap reads without RPC handshakes for every token. Maybe leases are issued by the local cache manager once a reader opens a shard; the lease is a short HMAC'd token valid for e.g. 10s. Eviction checks validate token expiration before deleting.
Indra: That avoids a global lease store. Runtime obtains a lease on mmap or streaming open and hands it to readers. When we rotate shards we write new artifact to temp path, then atomic-rename final. The manifest_digest in header acts as the swap guard for readers to assert they still point at expected digest.
Sam: One tradeoff: atomic rename across network filesystems can be flaky. Need fallback: write new artifact to a versioned name and then update a small pointer file (a 1-line JSON) with an atomic write+fsync. Pointer contains header digest and loader version. Runtimes can poll pointer first.
Jia: For HTTP/S object stores we do pointer semantics via a small metadata object (pointer key) and S3 atomicity model (overwrite object). We must also support conditional GETs using If-Match on pointer's etag to reduce races.
Clare: Warmup strategy should be explicit: cheap_probe|index-first|full-eager|stream-on-demand. We should surface which strategy was chosen in telemetry so Ops can correlate to p50/p99 and bytes-read.
Indra: Agreed. Instrumentation: warmup_strategy, header_probe_latency, bytes_prefetched, lease_hits, fallback_count. Also add a diagnostic header field "observability_hint" that runtime can set for debug builds.
Sam: Question: what about backwards compat with older safetensors without header? We need a compatibility shim: if no header present, treat as legacy and use full manifest-first. Document this in the loader API contract.
Jia: I'll prototype a range-index sidecar format (compact binary) and a small header parser that works for local mmap + HTTP. Will measure p50/p99 and bytes for small (<50MB) vs large models.
Clare: I'll draft lease lifecycle rules and eviction sequence: acquire lease on open, extend implicitly on read progress, revoke by marking pointer obsolete but wait for lease expiry + grace, then delete. Need to handle crash cases where lease not returned.
runtime-bot: Tests added: header_v2_parsing, pointer_race_sim, lease_expiry_recovery. CI job: eng-ml/header-v2 (#498). Failing tests on pointer_race_sim in CI.
Indra: OK action items: Jia spike for range-index + perf, Sam to write header schema doc + enums, Clare to write eviction/lease policy doc, I'll update RFC and add telemetry keys. Tickets: ENGML-901 (header-v2-spec), ENGML-902 (range-index-spike), ENGML-903 (lease-eviction-policy). Back to you all for comments — prefer concise replies here so we can merge spec next week. :thumbsup:
